stem.text: The temperature of a cup of tea, measured in degrees Celsius, is modeled by a twice-differentiable function H of time t, measured in minutes. It is known that \( H'(2) = 8 \). Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( H'(2) = 8 \) in the context of the problem.

answer_key.label: At time t = 2 minutes, the temperature of the tea is increasing at a rate of 8 degrees Celsius per minute.

worked_solution.text: \( H'(2) \) is the rate of change of the temperature of the tea at the instant t = 2, so it is measured in degrees Celsius per minute.
worked_solution.rule_named: derivative as a rate of change

worked_solution.text: The value is positive, so the temperature of the tea is increasing at that instant, by 8 degrees Celsius for each minute.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the derivative gives the direction

options.label: At time t = 2 minutes, the temperature of the tea is increasing at a rate of 8 degrees Celsius per minute.
At time t = 2 minutes, the temperature of the tea has changed by a total of 8 degrees Celsius.
options.derivation: the derivative value read as an amount, the total change in the quantity, rather than a rate

options.label: At time t = 2 minutes, the temperature of the tea is increasing at a rate of 8 minutes per degree Celsius.
options.derivation: the units assembled the wrong way round, time units over quantity units

options.label: Over the first 2 minutes, the temperature of the tea is increasing at a rate of 8 degrees Celsius per minute.
options.derivation: the instant replaced by the whole interval up to it, so the interpretation no longer says when the rate holds
